articles.title: How to escape our collective paralysis in ‘these uncertain times’
articles.summary:
Author Natasha Lennard discusses how to disrupt the ‘certainties’ that don’t serve us and how to fight back

At the onset of the Covid pandemic in 2020, journalist Natasha Lennard started noticing a constant thrum of collective apprehension, epitomized in the phrase “in these uncertain times”. The expression acknowledged we didn’t have solutions for many of society’s problems: a globally spreading virus, the rise of the far right and stark “haves v have-nots” inequalities. In the years since, that “uncertainty” hasn’t gone anywhere, risking enabling paralysis – not knowing where to start to fix things and therefore giving up before trying.

In her new book, On Un/Certainty: The Uses of Doubt in Dangerous Times, Lennard, who also was an organizer in the 2011 Occupy Wall Street movement, deconstructs the problematic nature of giving in to uncertainty. She also uses the Austrian-British philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein’s 1969 book On Certainty to question what is held as “certain” in today’s world, and who gets to make those calls.

Meanwhile, political tension in the US is mounting following federal investigations into opposition figures and heated pre-election rhetoric.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující volatilitu a zvýšený tlak na riziková aktiva, přičemž investoři budou nadále vyhodnocovat dopady technologického výprodeje.
archive.forecast_en: Continued volatility and heightened pressure on risk assets can be expected in the coming days as investors continue to assess the fallout from the tech sell-off.

archive.security_status_cs: Americké trhy a politickou scénu otřásá prudký výprodej v technologickém sektoru vyvolaný čínským modelem DeepSeek a rostoucí geopolitické napětí spojené s možnými vojenskými údery vůči Hútíům v Jemenu. Blížící se listopadové midterm volby navíc stupňují domácí polarizaci, což provázejí kontroverzní federální vyšetřování a vyostřená imigrační rétorika.

Furthermore, the upcoming November midterm elections are intensifying domestic polarization, accompanied by controversial federal investigations and heightened immigration rhetoric.
